fieldDescription: Steers your fleet while it's flying itself to something that's switched on in the Targets tab. By default that's planets, stars, jump points, gates and star systems. Holding a mouse button, the go-slow key, Sensor Burst or Interdiction Pulse gives you control back for that moment.
Slows down inside and just ahead of storming or signaling cells, then burns back up after. The game doesn't strike fleets that are moving slowly.
Goes around a storm on the way to the target if the detour is short enough. Otherwise it just slows down and goes through.

fieldName: Storm detour limit (percent of the leg)
fieldDescription: The longest detour around a storm it'll take, as a percent of the distance to the target.
After leaving a slipstream, it fights the sideways speed first and then turns back to the target right away.

Hops on a nearby slipstream when it flows toward the target and saves time, and gets off where the trip ends up shortest. Turned off, it won't hop on, but it still gets off a stream you end up in at the best point.
The biggest angle between the stream's flow and the direction to the target where it'll still get on.
It only gets on a slipstream when the trip takes at least this percent less time.
If you have the ability, it turns Reverse Polarity on before entering or crossing a slipstream that flows away from the target, and off after leaving. Outside a slipstream that's free.
Also turns Reverse Polarity on inside a slipstream that's carrying you away from the target. That costs fuel and CR like doing it by hand, so it's skipped when a ship's CR is below the cost.

Without a usable Reverse Polarity, it stays out of a slipstream on the way that doesn't flow toward the target. If the target's on this side it goes along the edge. If it's across, it crosses straight over at a gap or the weakest spot near the way, with Sustained Burn off.

Steers around star coronas, black hole event horizons and stars (pulsar beams aren't steered around). If your course is to a star, a black hole or a point inside a corona, it stops outside and ends the course there.
Extra distance it keeps from hazards and stars, on top of the fleet's radius.

fieldName: Slow down in asteroid belts and fields
fieldDescription: Slows down inside asteroid belts and fields, starting at braking distance before them, then burns back up after. Slow-moving fleets don't take asteroid impacts.

fieldName: Burn out of coronas and pulsar beams
fieldDescription: If a corona, a black hole or a pulsar beam holds the fleet back so it can't get closer to the target for 4 seconds, it turns Sustained Burn off for full acceleration. If that's not enough, it uses Emergency Burn, but only when every ship has the CR for it, so nothing takes damage. The game turns the Neutrino Detector off for it, like when you do it yourself. Close to the target, Sustained Burn goes off right away. With SEEKER's Enhanced Emergency Burn, it uses that one.

fieldName: Transverse Jump out of pulsar beams
fieldDescription: If a pulsar beam still holds the fleet after normal burn and Emergency Burn (or those can't be used), it uses Transverse Jump to get out into hyperspace. That costs fuel and CR like doing it by hand. It won't do it while you have Go Dark on. If your target is in that same system, the course gets cleared once you're out, so it doesn't fly you straight back into the beam.
Steers around hostile fleets you can see, that can see you and that are stronger than you. It'll fly straight past weaker ones.
A hostile fleet counts as stronger when its effective strength is above yours times this number.
How far it stays from stronger hostile fleets, added to both fleets' radii.

Turns Sustained Burn on for trips longer than 2000 units and 11 seconds, and back on if the game or another ability turned it off. Also while riding a slipstream with the flow (it goes off when you leave the stream). Not while slowing down, near a slipstream or with a stronger hostile fleet close by. It goes off again within 2000 units of the target, like the NPC fleets do. If you turn it off yourself, it stays off until your next target. With SEEKER's Enhanced Sustained Burn, it uses that one. In the Abyssal Depths it uses RAT's Abyssal Burn.

Jumps into and out of star systems without the jump dialog. You'll still get the dialog when the game would warn you about hostile fleets at the exit, ask about your transponder, or you're short on fuel, and for wormholes, unstable jump points and jump points with more than one exit. Fuel and jump pay are the same as a normal jump.
After you use Transverse Jump yourself, your course stays laid in but the fleet waits where it comes out until you resume it (the autopilot key, or click the target).

fieldName: Wait out pulsar beams at jump points
fieldDescription: If the other side of a jump point (or gravity well) is in a pulsar beam, the fleet stops short of it and waits until the beam has turned past, then jumps. After 10 days it jumps anyway.

A laid-in course goes through two gates of one network when that's at least the percent below and one light year shorter. This needs Travel through the Gate (Janus Device working, At the Gates finished), and it uses scanned active gates, plus gate beacons as exits only (like a Random Assortment of Things settlement with a Gate Beacon). It flies to the entry gate, goes through without the gate dialog at the game's fuel cost, and lays your course back in on the other side. With hostile fleets near the exit gate or not enough fuel, it skips the transit and lays your course back in. Laying in the same course again during a gate route flies direct. It's off while the Autopilot With Gates ability is on.

With AoTD Vaults of Knowledge and a Bifrost Control Center on a colony, gate routes also use Bifrost gates. The gate you go in through has to be supplied and not cooling down, and the one you come out of just can't be used already, same as in AoTD. A Bifrost transit costs no fuel and puts both gates on a 30-day cooldown, unless a hypershunt powers them.

With the Wormhole Scanner, gate routes also go through your wormhole termini when that's shorter. It goes through without the dialog at the game's wormhole fuel cost, and it skips a terminus that's still unstable. If your transponder is off, it won't route you to a terminus in a system with markets.
Gate routes won't use a gate in a system with a pulsar (game gates, gate beacons and Bifrost gates), since coming out there can drop you right in the beam.
It only uses gates when the way through them is at least this percent and one light year shorter.
Writes each steering change, why it isn't steering, the obstacles it found for each target and a status line every 10 seconds to starsector.log. Nothing shows up on screen.

defaultValue: Turn the autopilot on or off for each kind of thing you can fly to. It goes by what you're flying to right now, so on a course to another system, the jump points on the way count as jump points.

fieldDescription: Planets, moons and gas giants that don't have a colony.
Planets with a colony on them, yours or anybody else's.
Stars, neutron stars and black holes.
Stations with a market (faction stations, pirate and Pather bases, your own, etc.), plus any other station that isn't listed below.
The game's abandoned stations, the ones you can use for storage.
Derelict research stations you can salvage.
Derelict mining stations you can salvage.
Derelict orbital habitats you can salvage.
Derelict ships you can salvage or recover.
Supply, equipment, weapon and technology caches, and cargo pods.
Debris fields you can salvage.
Domain-era survey probes.
Derelict Domain-era survey ships.
Derelict Domain-era motherships.
Domain-era cryosleepers.
Derelict gatehaulers.
Coronal hypershunts at stars.
Stuff you can salvage that doesn't fit another switch, like Industrial Evolution's derelict stations and other mods' derelicts.
Comm relays, nav buoys and sensor arrays, makeshift ones too.
Stable locations where you can build a relay, buoy or array.
The warning beacons in hyperspace next to dangerous systems.
Anything that doesn't fit the other switches, like objects from other mods.
Jump points and wormhole termini.
Gates, gate beacons and Bifrost gates.
A course to a star system, or to a spot you picked on the map.
Fleets that are hostile to you, battlestations included.
Neutral and friendly fleets, like traders, patrols and your own fleets.
